description: A glossary of words a reader may need explained (feasts, offerings, offices, beliefs), keyed like data/names.json by Strong's number and lemma, copied from the source data. The reader shows each as a card in the panel and, in the Study view, explains the English it became when tapped. Like the name cards, these are editorial aids, not translation: they state the sense only and use no reader settings. Every entry is an AI draft until a named reviewer approves it.

senses.name: Sabbath
senses.note: The seventh day of the week, from Friday evening to Saturday evening, set apart for rest and for God by the law of Moses. Work was forbidden on it, and later teachers debated what counted as work.

senses.name: Sabbath
senses.note: The seventh day of the week, from Friday evening to Saturday evening, set apart for rest and for God by the law of Moses. Work was forbidden on it, and later teachers debated what counted as work.

senses.name: covenant
senses.note: A solemn binding agreement. In the Bible it is above all the relationship God makes with people, with promises and obligations: with Noah, with Abraham, with Israel at Sinai, and the new covenant the prophets announced.

senses.name: Passover
senses.note: The spring festival remembering the night Israel left Egypt, when the destroyer passed over houses marked with a lamb's blood. A lamb was killed and eaten with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

senses.name: Passover
senses.note: The spring festival remembering the night Israel left Egypt, when the destroyer passed over houses marked with a lamb's blood. A lamb was killed and eaten with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

senses.name: unleavened bread
senses.note: Bread made without yeast, eaten at Passover and through the seven-day Festival of Unleavened Bread that follows it, in memory of the hurried departure from Egypt.

senses.name: unleavened bread
senses.note: Bread made without yeast, eaten at Passover and through the seven-day Festival of Unleavened Bread that follows it, in memory of the hurried departure from Egypt.

senses.name: Pentecost
senses.note: The Greek name, meaning fiftieth, for the harvest Festival of Weeks, held fifty days after Passover. Jews from many lands gathered in Jerusalem for it.

senses.name: Festival of Booths
senses.note: Also called Tabernacles: the autumn festival at the end of harvest, when people lived for a week in shelters made of branches to remember Israel's years in the wilderness.

senses.name: circumcision
senses.note: The cutting away of the foreskin, the sign of God's covenant with Abraham, given to Jewish boys on the eighth day. The word can also stand for the Jewish people as a whole.

senses.name: synagogue
senses.note: A Jewish meeting place for prayer, reading and teaching the Scriptures, found in towns in the land of Israel and across the Roman world. The word can also mean the gathering itself.

senses.name: council
senses.note: The Sanhedrin, the highest Jewish court in Jerusalem, made up of chief priests, elders and teachers of the law and led by the high priest.

senses.name: tabernacle
senses.note: The sacred tent Israel carried through the wilderness, where God was present among the people and where the priests served, until the temple was built.

senses.name: atonement
senses.note: The covering or removal of sin so that people are put right with God, above all through the sacrifices of the yearly Day of Atonement.

senses.name: atoning sacrifice
senses.note: Words for the means by which sin is dealt with and people are put right with God. Scholars discuss whether they stress taking away sin or turning away God's anger. One of them also names the mercy seat on the ark of the covenant.

senses.name: atoning sacrifice
senses.note: Words for the means by which sin is dealt with and people are put right with God. Scholars discuss whether they stress taking away sin or turning away God's anger. One of them also names the mercy seat on the ark of the covenant.

senses.name: mercy seat
senses.note: The gold lid of the ark of the covenant, with a cherub at each end. On the Day of Atonement the high priest sprinkled blood on it for the sins of the people.

senses.name: sacrifice
senses.note: Something offered to God, often an animal killed and burned on an altar, given as worship, thanks, or to deal with sin.

senses.name: sacrifice
senses.note: Something offered to God, often an animal killed and burned on an altar, given as worship, thanks, or to deal with sin.

senses.name: altar
senses.note: A raised place, often of stone or earth, where sacrifices and offerings were made to God. The tabernacle and the temple had an altar for burnt offerings and a smaller one for incense.

senses.name: altar
senses.note: A raised place, often of stone or earth, where sacrifices and offerings were made to God. The tabernacle and the temple had an altar for burnt offerings and a smaller one for incense.

senses.name: incense
senses.note: Spices burned to give fragrant smoke, offered to God each day in the tabernacle and the temple. The Bible pictures prayers rising like incense.

senses.name: incense
senses.note: Spices burned to give fragrant smoke, offered to God each day in the tabernacle and the temple. The Bible pictures prayers rising like incense.

senses.name: priest
senses.note: One set apart to serve God at the altar, offering sacrifices for the people and teaching the law. In Israel the priests were descendants of Aaron.

senses.name: priest
senses.note: One set apart to serve God at the altar, offering sacrifices for the people and teaching the law. In Israel the priests were descendants of Aaron.

senses.name: chief priest
senses.note: The high priest, or one of the senior priests and leading priestly families in Jerusalem, who controlled the temple and sat on the council.

senses.name: tithe
senses.note: A tenth of crops, flocks or income, given to God and used to support the Levites and priests, the poor, and the festivals.

senses.name: firstfruits
senses.note: The first part of a harvest, offered to God as a sign that the whole harvest is God's gift. Paul uses it for the first of something more to come.

senses.name: Jubilee
senses.note: Every fiftieth year in the law of Moses, when land returned to its families, Israelite slaves went free, and fields were left unsown.

senses.name: ark
senses.note: A wooden chest. Above all the ark of the covenant, a gold-covered chest holding the tablets of the law, kept in the most holy place of the tabernacle and then the temple.

senses.name: cherubim
senses.note: Winged heavenly beings who guard God's presence. Gold figures of them stood over the ark of the covenant, and they were woven into the tabernacle's curtains.

senses.name: seraphim
senses.note: Winged heavenly beings, whose name may mean burning ones. Isaiah saw them calling to one another around God's throne.

senses.name: Nazirite
senses.note: A person set apart to God by a vow, who for its time drank no wine, did not cut their hair, and kept away from the dead.

senses.name: scribe
senses.note: An expert in the law of Moses and its interpretation, who copied, studied and taught it. Many were Pharisees.

senses.name: scribe
senses.note: An expert in the law of Moses and its interpretation, who copied, studied and taught it. Many were Pharisees.

senses.name: tax collector
senses.note: A local agent who collected taxes and tolls for Rome or for Herod's family, often charging more than was due. They were despised as cheats and collaborators.

senses.name: apostle
senses.note: Someone sent out with a message. Above all the twelve Jesus chose, and others such as Paul, sent to bear witness to Jesus and lead the church.

senses.name: demon
senses.note: An evil spirit, opposed to God, that can harm or take control of a person. In the Gospels Jesus drives them out with a word.

senses.name: Hades
senses.note: The Greek name for the realm of the dead, the place where the dead go. It translates the Hebrew Sheol.

senses.name: hell (Gehenna)
senses.note: The valley of Hinnom, outside Jerusalem, once a place of child sacrifice. Its name became a word for the place of final judgment and punishment.

senses.name: skin disease
senses.note: A word for several kinds of serious skin disease, not only what is called leprosy today. The law of Moses kept those who had it apart until a priest declared them clean.

senses.name: repentance
senses.note: A change of mind and heart that turns a person away from sin and back to God, shown in a changed life.

senses.name: repentance
senses.note: A change of mind and heart that turns a person away from sin and back to God, shown in a changed life.

senses.name: baptize
senses.note: To dip or wash in water. John the Baptist baptized people as a sign of repentance, and from the first the church has baptized those who come to believe.

senses.name: Hosanna
senses.note: A Hebrew cry meaning save us now, which became a shout of praise. Crowds shouted it as Jesus rode into Jerusalem.
